19	import java.util.Collection;

21	import org.springframework.orm.ObjectRetrievalFailureException;
22	import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.model.BaseEntity;
23	
24	/**
25	 * Utility methods for handling entities. Separate from the BaseEntity class mainly because of dependency on the
26	 * ORM-associated ObjectRetrievalFailureException.
27	 *
28	 * @author Juergen Hoeller
29	 * @author Sam Brannen
30	 * @see org.springframework.samples.petclinic.model.BaseEntity
31	 * @since 29.10.2003
32	 */
33	public abstract class EntityUtils {
34	
35	    /**
36	     * Look up the entity of the given class with the given id in the given collection.
37	     *
38	     * @param entities    the collection to search
39	     * @param entityClass the entity class to look up
40	     * @param entityId    the entity id to look up
41	     * @return the found entity
42	     * @throws ObjectRetrievalFailureException if the entity was not found
43	     */
44	    public static <T extends BaseEntity> T getById(Collection<T> entities, Class<T> entityClass, int entityId)
45	        throws ObjectRetrievalFailureException {
46	        for (T entity : entities) {
47	            if (entity.getId() == entityId && entityClass.isInstance(entity)) {
48	                return entity;
49	            }
50	        }
51	        throw new ObjectRetrievalFailureException(entityClass, entityId);
52	    }

## What I did

The named method `Owner::getTelephoneDisplay` doesn't exist yet — the change will add it. The one test in the suite (`AcceptanceTest.coreFormatsTelephoneDisplay`) is the acceptance test *for that change* and is red by design until it lands.

I found the reason a naive `getTelephoneDisplay` on `Owner` would carry too much: to format `+61412345678` → `+61 412 345 678` it must split the country calling code from the national digits, and that country-code knowledge (`NATIONAL_DIGITS_BY_COUNTRY` + a "longest matching code" lookup) lived **privately in `OwnerRestControllerV1`**. A direct implementation would have had to duplicate that table inside `Owner`.

This codebase already has a strong idiom: **`Owner` is the single source of domain/reference knowledge** (`CITY_REGION`, `REGION_POSTCODE_RANGE`, `regionOf`, `UNKNOWN_REGION`, `isPostcodeValid`), and the controller reads *through* `Owner` (`owner.getRegion()`, `Owner.UNKNOWN_REGION`, etc.). Each reference table is a private static map fronted by a small pure helper with a rich "single source … never re-derived elsewhere" javadoc.

So I moved the E.164 country-code knowledge onto `Owner`, mirroring the region block exactly:

- `Owner` now owns `NATIONAL_DIGITS_BY_COUNTRY` (private, documented single source), a private `countryCodeOf(...)` split helper, and a public `hasValidNationalLength(...)`.
- `OwnerRestControllerV1` deleted its duplicate table and private helper; `toE164` now calls `Owner.hasValidNationalLength(...)`, and its javadoc link was updated. The now-unused `java.util.Map` import was removed.

Nothing I added is dead code — the controller's existing validation exercises the new `Owner` members. This leaves `getTelephoneDisplay` to land as a thin instance getter that reuses `countryCodeOf` to split, then groups the national digits in threes — small and consistent with the other derived getters (`getAgeBand`, `getMembershipNumber`, `getLocality`).
